Commissioner Ottaviano Bellafonte: Captured after the heroes found his corrupt collection. He approved repairs that were never completed, including the Cistern Steps pump. Fenwick delivered gifts and Civic Loomworks invoices. Bellafonte hid an insurance ledger in the false bottom of the green-topped north alcove plinth. The emergency phrase is 'The collection is closed. I kept the last receipt.' He is vain, frightened, eager to retain small privileges, and afraid of physical harm. He asks for courtesy but has no leverage to demand terms. Under sufficient pressure he tells the truth. He does not know Merovanni, Dury, the Author, or what L.R.A. means.
Rudiger Fenwick: Broker for Civic Loomworks and Festooning. He delivered gifts and false completion reports to Bellafonte. His instructions use warm blue wax. He wants Bellafonte's ledger destroyed and to escape with his satchel. He knows company dispatch procedures and L.R.A. only as an account code. He does not know Merovanni, Dury, or the supernatural conspiracy. He is polite when in control, terse and pragmatic when threatened.
Lieutenant Hanae Petrovic: Honest Gold Button lieutenant coordinating the heroes' limited repair-fraud work letters. She can accept custody and evidence, give a receipt, keep the work letters active for the Bellafonte-Fenwick claim, and honor an earned reward. She cannot give universal warrants or command every city institution. She is direct and practical.
Melvin Corbin: Investigator of Vesk Aldermere's erasure. Reginald Veros dismissed him off-screen during the interval before the sting. Without his badge he is more independent and determined. He collaborates actively with the heroes through surveillance, discreet interviews, public records, sources, and careful case analysis. He does not solve dangerous scenes off-screen or claim official authority he no longer has.
